DEPARTMENT OF THE ARMY
MISSION AND INSTALLATION CONTRACTING COMMAND
MICC – FORT CALDER, KENTUCKY

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)
CUSTODIAL SERVICES
FORT CALDER, KENTUCKY

Section J, Attachment J-0001 to Solicitation W9124D-26-R-0019

Part 1 – General Information

1.1 General. This is a non-personal services contract to provide custodial services at Fort Calder, Kentucky. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government.

1.2 Description of Services. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform custodial services for the facilities listed in Technical Exhibit 1 (TE-1), Custodial Facility List, as defined in this PWS except for those items specified as Government-furnished property and services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this PWS.

1.3 Scope and Estimated Workload. The custodial workload consists of twenty-six (26) facilities totaling 593,210 gross square feet (GSF) in three service zones, as listed in TE-1. Square footages are gross building areas taken from the installation real property inventory and are provided for estimating purposes. The Contractor shall clean all interior areas of each listed facility unless an area is excluded in the TE-1 remarks or footnotes.

1.4 Period of Performance. The period of performance shall be one (1) 12-month base period and four (4) 12-month option periods, as follows:

PeriodDates
Phase-In1 September 2026 – 30 September 2026 (30 calendar days, no separate CLIN)
Base Period1 October 2026 – 30 September 2027
Option Period 11 October 2027 – 30 September 2028
Option Period 21 October 2028 – 30 September 2029
Option Period 31 October 2029 – 30 September 2030
Option Period 41 October 2030 – 30 September 2031

The Government may also require continued performance of services for up to six (6) months under FAR 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services. This extension is not an additional option period.

1.5 Hours of Operation. Normal Government duty hours are Monday through Friday, 0730 to 1630, excluding Federal holidays. Unless TE-1 states otherwise, custodial services in occupied office areas shall be performed between 1700 and 0500 so as not to interfere with the mission.

1.6 Recognized Holidays. New Year’s Day, Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday, Washington’s Birthday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth National Independence Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. Facilities with a “Daily (7 Days)” frequency are serviced on holidays.

Part 5 – Specific Tasks

5.1 Service Frequencies. Service frequencies stated in TE-1 are defined as follows. A service consists of all routine tasks in paragraph 5.2 for the entire facility.

TE-1 FrequencyDefinitionServices per Week
Daily (M–F)Once each workday, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays5
Daily (7 Days)Once each calendar day, seven days per week, including weekends and Federal holidays7
3x WeeklyMonday, Wednesday and Friday3
2x WeeklyTuesday and Thursday2
WeeklyOnce per week, on a day coordinated with the Building Custodian1

5.2 Routine Custodial Tasks. Each service shall include, at a minimum:

  1. Empty all trash receptacles and replace liners; remove trash and recyclables to the designated collection point.
  2. Clean and sanitize latrines, including toilets, urinals, sinks, counters, mirrors, partitions and floors; restock paper products and hand soap.
  3. Sweep and damp-mop resilient and hard-surface floors; vacuum carpeted traffic lanes and entrance mats.
  4. Spot clean entrance glass, doors, push plates, light switches and drinking fountains.
  5. Clean break rooms, including sinks, counters, tables and exterior surfaces of appliances.

5.3 Periodic Floor Care. Resilient floors shall be stripped and refinished semiannually and spray-buffed monthly. Carpets shall be hot-water extracted semiannually. Periodic floor care is included in the firm-fixed-price for each facility in TE-1.

5.4 Supplies. The Contractor shall furnish all cleaning supplies, paper products, hand soap and trash liners. Products shall meet the sustainable acquisition requirements of FAR Subpart 23.1.

5.5 Building Custodians. Each facility has a Government-designated Building Custodian who shall be the Contractor’s point of contact for access and scheduling. The COR will provide the list of Building Custodians at the post-award conference.

5.6 Infection Control. In Buildings 2105 and 2115, the Contractor shall use EPA-registered disinfectants and color-coded cleaning materials, and shall follow the facility infection control plan.

5.7 Simulation and Training Areas. In Building 1210, the Contractor shall use HEPA-filtered vacuums and shall not use liquid cleaners on simulator equipment.
